Structure tree of a nested result object

Source: R/utils_print.R
pr_tree.Rd

Print the elements of a list-based result as a tree, each with a short description such as <tibble 12 x 7>, <chr 3> "Age", "Sex", "Stage" or <ggplot>; clearer than str() for the nested lists that analysis functions return. Atomic vectors show their first values, as many as fit the console width, a data frame its column names, and a list left closed at max_depth its names with the value of each single one (an unnamed list an ellipsis). POSIXlt date-times display as equivalent POSIXct vectors. Sibling names line up in a column. Types and sizes are grey, values in the text colour with NA in red, and the names of elements that hold others bold; a classed list starts with its class as a chip. Closed previews restore methods for stored classed values; SPSS user-missing values display as NA.

Usage

pr_tree(x, max_depth = 3, max_items = 20, max_lines = 200, attrs = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A list or list-based object.

max_depth

Non-negative integer, or Inf. Levels below the root to show (default 3).

max_items

Non-negative integer, or Inf. Elements per node before the rest are summarised as "... n more", with their names (default 20).

max_lines

Non-negative integer, or Inf. Lines shown in all (default 200); a grey footer counts the rest.

attrs

Logical. Show extra attributes (default TRUE).

Value

The printed lines, invisibly.

Details

The object passed in always opens: a model fit lists its components, a data frame its columns and an S4 object its slots (as @name). Below it the tree descends into plain lists and into classed objects that also inherit from "list" (as c("eff_res", "list") does). Data frames, plots and other objects are leaves, and so are gt tables, RegR pages and htmltools tag lists, which are lists underneath; R6 and other classed environments show their class. Attributes other than names, class, dimensions, row names, srcref and those a type keeps for itself (factor levels, a time zone, value labels) are listed under an open node, marked attr, and named at the end of a closed node's line as [attr: name].

See also

Other print helpers: pr_badge(), pr_box(), pr_head(), pr_kv(), pr_note(), pr_section(), pr_spark(), pr_table()

Examples

res <- structure(
  list(Overall = list(table = data.frame(term = "Age", HR = 1.8),
                      method = "cox"),
       Subgroup = data.frame(term = c("Male", "Female"), HR = c(1.2, 1.4))),
  class = c("eff_res", "list"),
  analysis = list(n = 120, outcome = "DSS")
)
pr_tree(res)
#>  eff_res  <list 2>
#> ├─Overall  <list 2>
#> │ ├─table  <data.frame 1 x 2> term, HR
#> │ └─method <chr> "cox"
#> ├─Subgroup <data.frame 2 x 2> term, HR
#> └─attr analysis <list 2> n = 120, outcome = "DSS"
